mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in GDP growth below 1.5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls below 1.5% growth for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: If GDP growth remains below 1.5% for 6 months but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the industrial production index above 2% signals accelerating manufacturing output, which increases corporate earnings visibility and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises above 2% growth for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises above 2% for 3 months but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3.5% signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
